entries.meaning: Backyard has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The kids are out in the backyard.
We grilled in the backyard until it got dark.
Most of the backyards on this street back onto the creek.
Nobody wants a landfill in their own backyard.
The company found its best customers right in its own backyard.
The senator called the conflict a crisis in America's backyard.

senses.head: The open ground behind a house, often fenced
examples: The kids are out in the backyard.
We grilled in the backyard until it got dark.
Most of the backyards on this street back onto the creek.

senses.head: The area close to where you live or operate, thought of as your own territory
examples: Nobody wants a landfill in their own backyard.
The company found its best customers right in its own backyard.
The senator called the conflict a crisis in America's backyard.

entries.русский: задний двор, двор за домом; своя территория, задворки (перен.)
entries.contrast: Americans say backyard; the British say back garden.

entries.meaning: The piece of ground between a house and the street. ---
examples: He was out mowing the front yard at seven in the morning.
There's a big maple in the front yard.
All the front yards on the block are watered by timer.

entries.meaning: A long flexible tube for carrying water to a lawn or garden. ---
examples: Roll up the garden hose before somebody trips on it.
The garden hose is leaking right at the connector.
We keep two garden hoses, one front and one back.

entries.meaning: A plot of ground where food plants are grown. ---
examples: They put in a vegetable garden along the south fence.
Half the vegetable garden is tomatoes.
Vegetable gardens need at least six hours of sun.
entries.contrast: Russian огород is a vegetable garden; plain garden in American English usually means the flowers and shrubs.

entries.meaning: A planting box of soil built up above the level of the ground. ---
examples: He built a raised bed out of cedar boards.
The lettuce goes in the shady raised bed.
Four raised beds fit easily in that yard.

entries.meaning: The cutting of grass to keep a lawn short. ---
examples: Mowing takes him about an hour.
The lawn needs mowing twice a week in June.
I hired a kid down the street to do the mowing.

entries.meaning: The giving of water to plants. ---
examples: Early morning is the best time for watering.
The pots need watering every single day in August.
Can you take over the watering while we're gone?

entries.meaning: The work of gathering leaves or smoothing soil with a rake. ---
examples: Raking leaves is a whole weekend around here.
My shoulders are sore from all that raking.
The yard still needs one more round of raking.

entries.meaning: The spreading of bark, straw, or leaves over soil to hold moisture in. ---
examples: Mulching cuts my watering in half.
We finished the mulching on Sunday afternoon.
Heavy mulching keeps the weeds from coming up.

entries.meaning: The practice of letting plant waste rot down into food for the soil. ---
examples: The city has a class on backyard composting.
Composting got rid of most of our kitchen trash.
She's been composting for twenty years.

entries.meaning: The regular work of feeding, cutting, and watering a lawn. ---
examples: They pay a service for lawn care.
Lawn care around here means watering three times a week.
He knows more about lawn care than anyone on the block.

entries.meaning: Outdoor chores like mowing, raking, and trimming around a house. ---
examples: I've got a ton of yard work this weekend.
He does yard work to stay out of the house.
Saturday is for yard work and nothing else.

entries.meaning: Grass, leaves, and branches thrown out after garden work. ---
examples: Yard waste goes in the green bin.
The town picks up yard waste on Thursdays.
We had six bags of yard waste after the storm.

entries.meaning: A heap of rotting plant material kept for feeding the soil. ---
examples: Throw those weeds on the compost pile.
The compost pile steams on cold mornings.
He turns the compost pile with a pitchfork every few weeks.

entries.meaning: A light bagged mix used for growing plants in containers. ---
examples: Pick up a bag of potting soil while you're out.
Never use garden dirt where you need potting soil.
This potting soil holds water way too long.
entries.русский: грунт для рассады и комнатных растений
entries.contrast: Uncountable: a bag of potting soil, never a potting soil. The British call it potting compost.

entries.meaning: A liquid or powder added to water to feed potted plants. ---
examples: Add a capful of plant food every other watering.
The plant food is under the sink.
Too much plant food will burn the roots.

entries.meaning: Light brown decayed moss mixed into soil to hold moisture. ---
examples: Work some peat moss into that sandy bed.
A bale of peat moss costs about fifteen dollars.
Peat moss makes the soil more acidic.

entries.meaning: Ground animal bone used as a slow fertilizer, especially for bulbs. ---
examples: Put a spoonful of bone meal in each hole.
Bone meal is what my grandmother swore by for tulips.
The dog dug up everything I treated with bone meal.

entries.meaning: White volcanic granules mixed into soil to keep it loose and draining. ---
examples: Those little white specks in the mix are perlite.
Add a couple handfuls of perlite for the cuttings.
Perlite keeps the pot from staying soggy.

entries.meaning: A light flaky mineral mixed into soil to hold water and air. ---
examples: Cover the seeds with a thin layer of vermiculite.
Vermiculite holds water better than perlite does.
The starting mix is peat and vermiculite.

entries.meaning: Crumbly dark material made of leaves that have rotted down. ---
examples: Two years in a pile turns leaves into leaf mold.
He digs leaf mold into every bed in the fall.
Leaf mold smells like the floor of a forest.
entries.contrast: American mold, British mould — same word, different spelling.

entries.meaning: Small pieces of chopped wood spread on paths and around plants. ---
examples: The tree crew dumped a pile of wood chips for free.
We put wood chips down the whole side path.
Wood chips break down slower than bark.
entries.contrast: Used in the plural as a material: some wood chips, not a wood chip.

entries.meaning: The cut grass left behind after mowing a lawn. ---
examples: Leave the grass clippings on the lawn as fertilizer.
He bagged the grass clippings for the compost.
Wet grass clippings clog the mower.
entries.contrast: Always plural: the grass clippings, never a grass clipping.

entries.meaning: Seed spread on bare ground to grow a lawn. ---
examples: Throw some grass seed on that bald spot.
The grass seed won't come up until it warms up.
Birds ate half the grass seed I put down.

entries.meaning: A low spreading plant grown to cover bare soil. ---
examples: Creeping thyme makes a nice ground cover between the stones.
We need a ground cover for that slope.
Most shade-tolerant ground covers spread slowly.

entries.meaning: A small paper envelope of seeds sold for planting. ---
examples: The seed packet says thin to six inches.
I have a shoebox full of old seed packets.
Check the date on the back of the seed packet.

entries.meaning: A shallow plastic tray with small cells for starting seedlings. ---
examples: The peppers are up in the seed tray already.
Put the seed tray on the windowsill.
She washes and reuses the seed trays every year.

entries.meaning: A mailed or online listing of seeds and plants a company sells. ---
examples: The seed catalogs start showing up in January.
He circles half the seed catalog and orders three things.
That seed catalog has forty kinds of tomatoes.
entries.contrast: American catalog, British catalogue.

entries.meaning: A piece of stem cut from a plant and rooted to grow a new one. ---
examples: She rooted a cutting from her mother's rose bush.
Take cuttings about four inches long.
Half the cuttings took, half rotted.

entries.meaning: Graft has 3 distinct senses.
examples: You can see the graft right above the soil line.
The graft never took, so he tried again in spring.
All the grafts on that apple tree are different varieties.
The burn needed a skin graft.
Surgeons took the graft from her own hip.
Both grafts healed without infection.
The mayor went to prison for graft.
The city was once famous for graft and kickbacks.
Reporters spent a year documenting the graft.

senses.head: A shoot joined onto another plant so the two grow as one
examples: You can see the graft right above the soil line.
The graft never took, so he tried again in spring.
All the grafts on that apple tree are different varieties.

senses.head: A piece of skin, bone, or tissue moved to another place on the body
examples: The burn needed a skin graft.
Surgeons took the graft from her own hip.
Both grafts healed without infection.

senses.head: The use of a public position to get money dishonestly
examples: The mayor went to prison for graft.
The city was once famous for graft and kickbacks.
Reporters spent a year documenting the graft.

entries.русский: прививка (растения); трансплантат, пересадка ткани; коррупция, взяточничество

entries.meaning: A stem that creeps sideways underground and sends up new plants. ---
examples: Mint spreads by rhizomes, so keep it in a pot.
Split the rhizome with a sharp knife.
Those rhizomes went straight under the sidewalk.
entries.contrast: The h is silent: rh- is just R, as in rhyme.

entries.meaning: A small shoot or twig cut from a plant, usually an herb. ---
examples: Add a sprig of rosemary to the pan.
She cut a few sprigs of mint for the pitcher.
One sprig of thyme is plenty.

entries.meaning: A thin curling growth a climbing plant uses to hold on. ---
examples: The pea tendrils have grabbed the string already.
A tendril had wrapped itself around the railing.
Cucumber tendrils will pull down a weak trellis.

entries.meaning: All the roots of a plant taken together. ---
examples: Bamboo has a root system that will wreck a patio.
The tree's root system goes out farther than its branches.
Shallow root systems dry out fast.

entries.meaning: The mass of roots and soil that comes out with a plant when it is moved. ---
examples: Loosen the root ball before you set it in the hole.
The root ball was completely dried out.
Dig a hole twice as wide as the root ball.

entries.meaning: A plant that dies back in winter and comes up again year after year. ---
examples: Hostas are the easiest perennial I know.
She filled the shady bed with perennials.
That perennial has come back for nine years.

entries.meaning: A plant that grows, flowers, and dies all in one season. ---
examples: I put a flat of annuals in the window boxes every May.
Marigold is an annual, so it won't come back.
Annuals bloom all summer if you keep them watered.

entries.meaning: A plant that grows leaves the first year and flowers the second. ---
examples: Foxglove is a biennial, so be patient.
Biennials are worth the wait.
That biennial finally bloomed this June.
entries.contrast: Biennial means every two years; biannual means twice a year.

entries.meaning: Hybrid has 3 distinct senses.
examples: This tomato is a hybrid bred for disease resistance.
Seeds saved from a hybrid rarely come out the same.
Most of the corn in the store is from hybrids.
They traded the pickup for a hybrid to save on gas.
Hybrids get much better mileage in city traffic.
The dealership had one hybrid left on the lot.
The show is a hybrid of talk show and game show.
Their schedule is a hybrid: three days in the office, two at home.
This bike is a hybrid, part road bike and part mountain bike.

senses.head: A plant bred from two different varieties
examples: This tomato is a hybrid bred for disease resistance.
Seeds saved from a hybrid rarely come out the same.
Most of the corn in the store is from hybrids.

senses.head: A car that runs on both a gasoline engine and an electric motor
examples: They traded the pickup for a hybrid to save on gas.
Hybrids get much better mileage in city traffic.
The dealership had one hybrid left on the lot.

senses.head: Something that combines two different types or styles
examples: The show is a hybrid of talk show and game show.
Their schedule is a hybrid: three days in the office, two at home.
This bike is a hybrid, part road bike and part mountain bike.

entries.русский: гибрид; гибридный автомобиль; гибрид, сочетание (двух разных вещей)

entries.meaning: Green leaves and plants taken together. ---
examples: The porch is buried in greenery by July.
She added some greenery to the arrangement.
There's not much greenery on that side of the house.

entries.meaning: A planting of bushes growing together. ---
examples: The ball went into the shrubbery.
He trimmed the shrubbery along the walk.
Birds nest in that shrubbery every spring.

entries.meaning: A prickly bush of the blackberry or raspberry kind. ---
examples: The back corner is nothing but brambles.
He cut a path through the bramble with a machete.
Those brambles will take over if you let them.

entries.meaning: A weed with hairy leaves that sting the skin. ---
examples: I grabbed a nettle and my hand burned for an hour.
Nettles love rich damp soil.
Wear gloves — that whole bed is full of nettles.

entries.meaning: A prickly weed with purple flowers and seeds that blow away. ---
examples: Pull the thistle before it goes to seed.
Thistles come right back if you leave the root.
One thistle turns into fifty by next summer.
entries.contrast: The t is silent: THIS-uhl, like whistle.

entries.meaning: A big leafy tree planted to give shade. ---
examples: Plant a shade tree on the west side of the house.
The shade tree out front drops leaves for a month.
Those shade trees cut our cooling bill in half.

entries.meaning: A machine that blows a strong stream of air to clear leaves. ---
examples: Somebody fires up a leaf blower at seven every morning.
The battery leaf blower is a lot quieter.
Half the town runs leaf blowers in October.

entries.meaning: A powered tool with a long toothed blade for shaping hedges. ---
examples: Run the hedge trimmer along the top to even it out.
The hedge trimmer is in the shed with the extension cord.
Cordless hedge trimmers have gotten pretty good.

entries.meaning: A machine that cuts grass and weeds with a spinning nylon line. ---
examples: Use the string trimmer along the fence line.
The string trimmer is out of line again.
Both string trimmers need new spools.
entries.contrast: Most Americans call it a weed whacker or a weed eater in everyday speech.

entries.meaning: The everyday name for a string trimmer. ---
examples: Can I borrow your weed whacker this weekend?
He went after the ditch with a weed whacker.
The weed whacker won't start when it's cold.

entries.meaning: A hand tool with two curved blades for cutting small branches. ---
examples: Hand me the pruning shears — this cane is done.
The pruning shears need sharpening.
Wipe the pruning shears with alcohol between plants.
entries.contrast: Always plural, like scissors: a pair of pruning shears, even though Russian секатор is singular.

entries.meaning: A small curved saw for cutting branches too thick for shears. ---
examples: That limb needs a pruning saw.
A folding pruning saw fits right in your back pocket.
Both pruning saws cut on the pull stroke.

entries.meaning: A cutting tool with two long handles for thick branches. ---
examples: Get the loppers — the shears won't go through that.
The loppers are hanging in the garage.
These loppers will take a branch an inch and a half thick.
entries.contrast: Always plural: a pair of loppers, never a lopper.

entries.meaning: A short sturdy fork with flat tines for digging and loosening soil. ---
examples: Work the compost in with a garden fork.
A garden fork is better than a shovel in heavy clay.
He bent two garden forks on those rocks.

entries.meaning: A lawn mower with a seat that the operator drives. ---
examples: You need a riding mower for two acres.
The riding mower is in the shed under a tarp.
Used riding mowers go fast around here.

entries.meaning: A tool or machine that cuts a clean line where a lawn meets a walk or bed. ---
examples: Run the edger along the driveway last.
A sharp edger makes the whole yard look finished.
They sell manual edgers for about thirty dollars.

entries.meaning: A flat frame of crossed strips that a climbing plant grows up. ---
examples: Tie the vine loosely to the trellis.
The trellis blew over in the first storm.
Both trellises are covered in clematis by June.

entries.meaning: A container of flowers hung from a hook or bracket. ---
examples: A hanging basket dries out twice as fast as a pot.
She hung a hanging basket on each porch post.
The store had hanging baskets on sale for Mother's Day.

entries.meaning: A long shallow container of plants fixed under a window. ---
examples: The window box is full of petunias.
He built a cedar window box for the kitchen.
The window boxes have to be watered every evening.

entries.meaning: A low box with a clear lid that protects young plants from frost. ---
examples: The lettuce lives in the cold frame until April.
Prop the cold frame open on warm days.
He built two cold frames out of old storm windows.

entries.meaning: A waist-high table used for filling pots and working with plants. ---
examples: The potting bench is buried under empty containers.
He built a potting bench out of scrap lumber.
Most potting benches have a shelf underneath.

entries.meaning: A small outbuilding where tools and supplies are kept. ---
examples: The mower lives in the garden shed.
There's a wasp nest in the garden shed again.
Both garden sheds need new roofs.

entries.meaning: An electric lamp that gives plants the light they need indoors. ---
examples: Start the seedlings under a grow light in February.
The grow light hangs a few inches over the tray.
LED grow lights barely use any power.

entries.meaning: A large container that catches roof runoff for watering plants. ---
examples: The rain barrel fills up in one good storm.
He put a rain barrel under each downspout.
Two rain barrels get us through most dry spells.
entries.contrast: Americans say rain barrel; the British say water butt.

entries.meaning: An arched garden structure that vines are trained over. ---
examples: They got married under a rose arbor.
The arbor marks the entrance to the back garden.
Both arbors need repainting.
entries.contrast: American arbor, British arbour.

entries.meaning: An open frame of posts and crossbeams that shades a walk or patio. ---
examples: Grapevines cover the whole pergola by August.
They built a pergola over the back patio.
Cedar pergolas hold up better than pine.
entries.contrast: The stress is on the first syllable: PUR-guh-luh.

entries.meaning: Flat split stone used for paths and patios. ---
examples: They laid a flagstone path from the driveway.
One flagstone cracked over the winter.
Moss grows in the gaps between the flagstones.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A low fence of upright pointed boards with gaps between them. ---
examples: A white picket fence runs across the front.
The picket fence needs painting every few years.
Roses grow along both picket fences.

entries.meaning: A low wall built to hold back soil on a slope. ---
examples: They put in a stone retaining wall to level the yard.
The retaining wall is starting to bow out.
Two low retaining walls turned the hill into terraces.

entries.meaning: A border of brick, stone, or plastic set along a bed or path. ---
examples: Brick edging keeps the mulch off the lawn.
He put plastic edging around every bed.
The edging has heaved up over the winter.

entries.meaning: A small statue of a bearded man used as a yard ornament. ---
examples: There's a garden gnome under the birdbath.
Somebody stole the garden gnome off the porch.
She has eleven garden gnomes and counting.
entries.contrast: The g in gnome is silent: NOHM.

entries.meaning: A pond, fountain, or small waterfall built into a garden. ---
examples: They put in a small water feature by the patio.
The water feature runs on a little pump.
Water features attract more birds than a feeder does.
entries.русский: декоративный водоём или фонтан в саду

entries.meaning: A store that sells plants, soil, and garden supplies. ---
examples: The garden center is packed every Saturday in May.
I got the tomato starts at the garden center.
Both garden centers in town close for the winter.
entries.contrast: American center, British centre.

entries.meaning: A small planting of cooking herbs. ---
examples: The herb garden is right outside the kitchen door.
Mint took over half the herb garden.
Herb gardens do fine in pots on a balcony.
entries.contrast: In American English the h in herb is silent: URB gar-duhn, not HURB.

entries.meaning: A small garden of vegetables and herbs grown for the household. ---
examples: She keeps a kitchen garden right off the back steps.
A kitchen garden pays for itself in a season.
The old farmhouse had two kitchen gardens.

entries.meaning: A garden of stones planted with small tough plants that like dry soil. ---
examples: The slope became a rock garden.
Nothing but weeds grows in that rock garden now.
Rock gardens need almost no watering.

entries.meaning: A shared piece of land divided into plots that people rent to grow food. ---
examples: We got a plot at the community garden on Elm.
The community garden has a waiting list two years long.
The city runs four community gardens.

entries.meaning: A public garden where many kinds of plants are grown and labeled. ---
examples: The botanical garden is free on Tuesdays.
We spent the afternoon at the botanical garden.
Most big cities have botanical gardens.

entries.meaning: A park where trees are grown and studied. ---
examples: The arboretum has a hundred kinds of maple.
We walk the arboretum every fall for the color.
University arboretums are usually open to the public.
entries.contrast: The plural is arboretums or, more formally, arboreta.

entries.meaning: A natural skill for making plants grow well. ---
examples: She has a real green thumb.
I do not have a green thumb — I've killed three cactuses.
It takes a green thumb to keep orchids blooming.
entries.contrast: The b in thumb is silent, and the British say green fingers instead.

entries.meaning: The time of year when things are put in the ground. ---
examples: The nursery hires extra people for planting season.
Fall is the better planting season for trees.
We've missed two planting seasons in a row.

entries.meaning: A numbered region based on how cold the winter gets, used to pick plants. ---
examples: We're in hardiness zone six.
Check the hardiness zone on the tag before you buy.
The map splits the country into thirteen hardiness zones.

entries.meaning: A system of thin tubes that drips water slowly right at the roots. ---
examples: Drip irrigation cut our water bill way down.
He put drip irrigation in all four raised beds.
With drip irrigation the leaves stay dry.

entries.meaning: A porous hose that lets water seep out along its whole length. ---
examples: Snake a soaker hose down the middle of the row.
The soaker hose is buried under the mulch.
Two soaker hoses cover the whole bed.

entries.meaning: A set of buried pipes and pop-up heads that waters a lawn automatically. ---
examples: The sprinkler system comes on at five a.m.
We had the sprinkler system blown out before the freeze.
New sprinkler systems run off a phone app.

entries.meaning: The pulling of small plugs of soil out of a lawn to let in air and water. ---
examples: The lawn is due for aeration this fall.
Aeration helps most on hard clay.
They charge about a hundred dollars for aeration.

entries.meaning: The removal of faded flowers so a plant keeps blooming. ---
examples: A little deadheading keeps the petunias going all summer.
She does the deadheading with her morning coffee.
Without deadheading they set seed and quit.

entries.meaning: The pulling out of extra seedlings so the rest have room. ---
examples: The carrots need thinning or you'll get nothing but tops.
Thinning feels wasteful, but it doubles the crop.
Do the thinning when the plants are two inches tall.

entries.meaning: The growing of new plants from seeds, cuttings, or division. ---
examples: Propagation by cuttings is the fastest way to fill a bed.
The class covers seed starting and propagation.
She keeps a whole shelf for propagation.

entries.meaning: The carrying of pollen to a flower so it can make fruit or seed. ---
examples: No bees, no pollination, no squash.
You can do the pollination by hand with a small brush.
Wind handles the pollination for corn.

entries.meaning: The process by which green plants make food out of light, air, and water. ---
examples: Leaves in deep shade barely do any photosynthesis.
Photosynthesis slows down when it gets too hot.
Dust on the leaves cuts down photosynthesis.

entries.meaning: A trained expert in growing plants. ---
examples: The city horticulturist picked the street trees.
Ask a horticulturist before you cut that back.
Two horticulturists run the whole display garden.

entries.meaning: Someone whose job is designing and taking care of yards and grounds. ---
examples: We hired a landscaper to redo the front.
The landscaper said the soil had to be replaced.
Landscapers are booked solid all spring.

entries.meaning: A person who maintains the lawns and grounds of a large property. ---
examples: The groundskeeper has the field cut by six in the morning.
Talk to the groundskeeper about the sprinklers.
The campus employs six groundskeepers.

entries.meaning: A specialist in the care and pruning of trees. ---
examples: Get an arborist to look at that split trunk.
The arborist said the oak could be saved.
Certified arborists charge more, and they're worth it.
entries.русский: арборист, специалист по уходу за деревьями
entries.contrast: Americans hire an arborist; the British often say tree surgeon.

entries.meaning: Soft decay in a plant caused by too much moisture or disease. ---
examples: The bulbs sat in wet soil and went to rot.
Root rot killed both of my houseplants.
Cut away the rot and repot what's left.

entries.meaning: A product sprayed on unwanted plants to kill them. ---
examples: Don't use weed killer that close to the vegetables.
The weed killer took three days to work.
Most weed killers won't touch a dandelion root.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: An unusually large harvest. ---
examples: We had a bumper crop of zucchini and gave most of it away.
The wet spring gave everybody a bumper crop.
Two bumper crops in a row is almost unheard of.

entries.meaning: A tree kept tiny in a shallow pot by careful pruning. ---
examples: His bonsai is older than he is.
A bonsai has to be watered almost every day.
She keeps four bonsai on the windowsill.
entries.contrast: The plural is usually bonsai, unchanged.

entries.meaning: A shrub clipped into a decorative shape. ---
examples: There's a topiary shaped like a rabbit by the gate.
The topiaries get trimmed twice a summer.
One overgrown topiary is just a bush again.

entries.meaning: Growing plants in water and nutrients instead of soil. ---
examples: The lettuce at that farm is all hydroponics.
Hydroponics uses far less water than field growing.
He got into hydroponics to grow greens in the basement.
entries.contrast: Ends in -s but takes a singular verb: hydroponics is expensive to set up.

entries.meaning: A panel of thin strips crossed in a diamond pattern, used for screens and climbing plants. ---
examples: He nailed a lattice under the porch to hide the crawl space.
The clematis has covered the whole lattice.
Vinyl lattices don't rot the way wood ones do.

entries.meaning: A light cloth laid over plants to hold in warmth and keep insects off.
examples: Throw a row cover over the beans before the frost.
The row cover is held down with bricks.
Row covers have to come off once the plants flower.
entries.contrast: Row here rhymes with go, not with cow.
